query: Can a client be penalised for breaching index derivative position limits intraday?
answer_passage:
4.7. On the day of expiry of options contracts, the breaches of aforesaid position limits
shall additionally attract penalty/additional surveillance deposit, as decided jointly
by Stock Exchanges.
reference_answer: Yes, on options expiry days, from December 6, 2025 -- breaches of the intraday FutEq limits attract penalty or an additional surveillance deposit (circular 122). Circular 41 had previously ruled out any penalty for intraday breaches of the older notional limits.
stale_trap: SEBI-41 rules out any penalty for intraday breaches 'until further directions' -- true when written in March 2025, superseded that September

query: How did the treatment of intraday position limit breaches for index derivatives change during 2025?
answer_passage:
However, there shall be no penalty for breach of existing position limits intraday
and such intraday breaches shall not be considered as violations, until further
directions. || 4.7. On the day of expiry of options contracts, the breaches of aforesaid position limits
shall additionally attract penalty/additional surveillance deposit, as decided jointly
by Stock Exchanges.
reference_answer: In March 2025 circular 41 required intraday monitoring from April 1 but ruled out penalties. In September 2025 circular 122 set intraday FutEq limits and made expiry-day breaches penalisable from December 6, 2025.
stale_trap: the two circulars never cite each other and their subject lines differ, so nothing links them but the topic

query: Why can equity index funds only borrow for under-executed sell trades from August 2026 onwards?
answer_passage:
It is clarified that borrowings by equity-oriented index funds and equity-oriented
ETFs on account of under execution of sell trades on the Stock Exchange in terms
of Regulation 42(1) of SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026 is permissible only
for the purpose of participation by such funds in the Closing Auction Session || 6.1. The framework for CAS outlined at para 4 shall be implemented in the cash
segment from August 03, 2026.
reference_answer: Because that borrowing is permitted only to participate in the Closing Auction Session (circular 6961), and CAS begins in the cash segment on August 3, 2026 (circular 2765).
stale_trap: the borrowing rule names no date, and the date sits in a circular from a different department

query: Before September 2026, which FPIs were exempt from furnishing investor group details?
answer_passage:
“FPIs that invest exclusively in Government Securities under Fully Accessible
Route shall not be required to furnish investor group details.”
reference_answer: Only FPIs investing exclusively in Government Securities under the Fully Accessible Route. Circular 20296 widened this to all FPIs investing only in Government Securities.
stale_trap: the modified wording sits a few paragraphs below and drops the Fully Accessible Route condition

query: What were the financial result submission timelines for listed municipalities before the relaxation?
answer_passage:
(a) The listed entities shall prepare and submit half yearly un-audited financial
results to the stock exchange as soon as the same are available but within forty
five days of the end of the first half year. || (a) The listed entities shall submit annual audited financial results for the financial
year, within sixty days from the end of the financial year along with the audit
report.
reference_answer: Forty-five days from the end of the first half year for unaudited half-yearly results, and sixty days from the end of the financial year for audited annual results. Circular 18526 relaxed these to sixty and ninety days.
stale_trap: the relaxed timelines of sixty and ninety days are quoted immediately afterwards in near-identical wording

query: Is probate of a will still needed to transmit securities?
answer_passage:
Removal of mandatory requirement of Probate of Will, in line with recent

reference_answer: No. Circular 17111 removed the mandatory probate requirement, in line with recent amendments to succession laws.
